mechanism_inventory: missing solvency check / liquidation threshold validation (vault may not actually be underwater)
closeRatio bounds not enforced — allows 0 or overflow values
settlement data injection via user-supplied bytes — attacker controls the settlement callback path
missing access control — any EOA can call execLiquidationCall on any vault
stale accounting snapshot — interest not accrued before health check, allowing premature or incorrect liquidation
missing invariant enforcement on closeRatio cap (no check that closeRatio <= 1e18 or equivalent)
wrong lifecycle ordering — liquidation proceeds before verifying vault is actually insolvent
victim accounting direction — remaining margin sent to vault.recipient, which could be address(0) or attacker-controlled
hook caller or hook-timing mismatch — LiquidationLogic.liquidate may invoke callbacks into untrusted hook contracts
external-call failure / DoS — settlement callback to attacker-supplied contract can revert or drain gas

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: execLiquidationCall is permissionless and delegates entirely to LiquidationLogic.liquidate with no on-entry solvency check visible in PredyPool.sol. The closeRatio parameter is passed through unconstrained — no bounds check (e.g., 0 < closeRatio <= 1e18) appears in PredyPool.sol. If LiquidationLogic.liquidate does not enforce a strict closeRatio bound or does so incorrectly, an attacker can pass closeRatio=0 (no-op liquidation that still extracts liquidation bonus) or closeRatio>1e18 (over-liquidation beyond position size) against any vault.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged EOA, permissionless — no role or allowance needed.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker calls execLiquidationCall(victimVaultId, 0 or oversized closeRatio, settlementData). 2. LiquidationLogic.liquidate executes without a guard in PredyPool.sol on closeRatio bounds. 3. If closeRatio=0 causes a 0-size close that still pays out liquidation reward, attacker extracts bonus with no position closed. If closeRatio >> 1e18, position is over-closed, wiping more collateral than owed.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Vault owner (victim) loses collateral beyond what a fair partial liquidation should take.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Liquidator/attacker receives excess liquidation premium or unearned bonus.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: The only visible guard in PredyPool.sol is nonReentrant. No closeRatio range validation is present in the in-scope source. The burden of proof that LiquidationLogic.liquidate enforces bounds belongs to harness review — source of that library is not provided.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: The settlement path is controlled by attacker-supplied bytes settlementData. This data is passed to LiquidationLogic.liquidate which presumably calls into a settlement contract. The settlement contract address or parameters within settlementData can be crafted to redirect token flows, invoke malicious callbacks, or cause denial of service for legitimate liquidators.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged EOA; attacker crafts settlementData to point to a contract they control.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker deploys malicious settlement contract implementing ISettlement. 2. Attacker calls execLiquidationCall(victimVaultId, closeRatio, maliciousSettlementData). 3. LiquidationLogic.liquidate calls into attacker-controlled settlement contract. 4. Settlement contract may: (a) revert after state changes (griefing/DoS), (b) re-enter via the locker mechanism to call take() and drain tokens, or (c) manipulate the oracle mid-liquidation.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol LPs and vault owners — griefing prevents legitimate liquidations, or funds are drained via malicious callback.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker may extract tokens or block competitors from liquidating.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: ISettlement is imported but its validation is not shown in PredyPool.sol. The take() function enforces onlyByLocker, suggesting a locking mechanism exists — but whether the locker is set to the settlement contract during liquidation (enabling take() calls) is unresolved without LiquidationLogic source.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: vault.recipient is set by the vault owner (updateRecepient). During liquidation, remaining margin is sent to vault.recipient. If recipient is address(0) per NatSpec ('if recipient is zero address, protocol never transfers margin'), the remaining margin after liquidation is silently swallowed rather than returned to the vault owner, creating an effective fund loss for the vault owner even after a valid liquidation that leaves surplus collateral.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: No attacker required — this is a design-level loss for vault owners who forget to set recipient or set it to zero intentionally. An adversary can exploit this by front-running updateRecepient calls and leaving recipient=0.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Vault owner has not set recipient (default address(0)). 2. Vault becomes unhealthy. 3. Anyone calls execLiquidationCall. 4. Post-liquidation surplus margin is not returned to owner because recipient==0 causes the protocol to suppress the transfer. 5. Vault owner loses their remaining margin.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Vault owner loses surplus collateral that would otherwise be returned.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Protocol retains unclaimed funds (or they are locked in the contract permanently).
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: The NatSpec explicitly documents address(0) suppresses transfer. This is a real fund-loss vector for vault owners. It affects a different state variable (vault.recipient) and a different victim (vault owner post-liquidation surplus) than the closeRatio mechanism.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: closeRatio=0 or closeRatio > 1e18 admitted by PredyPool.sol — no bounds check in visible source
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: execLiquidationCall passes closeRatio directly to LiquidationLogic.liquidate with no validation in PredyPool.sol
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does LiquidationLogic.liquidate enforce 0 < closeRatio <= 1e18 before using it? Source of LiquidationLogic not provided.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Vault owner loses excess collateral if closeRatio can exceed 1e18

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Stale interest / accounting snapshot before solvency check — liquidation proceeds without accruing interest first, potentially allowing premature liquidation of a vault that would be healthy after accrual, or preventing liquidation of a vault that becomes underwater only after accrual
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: No accrueInterest() call is visible in execLiquidationCall in PredyPool.sol; interest accrual is standard in lending protocols before health checks
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does LiquidationLogic.liquidate internally accrue interest before computing health? Not resolvable from PredyPool.sol source alone.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Vault owner if prematurely liquidated on stale (inflated) collateral values; lenders if insolvent position is not liquidated timely
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Liquidator if they can trigger premature liquidation

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Settlement data injection enabling reentrancy via take() during liquidation callback
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: ISettlement import present; take() enforces onlyByLocker; PredyPool uses ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable but nonReentrant only on execLiquidationCall itself — if settlement callback calls another contract that calls back into PredyPool via a non-nonReentrant path, reentrancy may be possible
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Is the locker set to the settlement contract during LiquidationLogic.liquidate, enabling take() calls? Does any non-nonReentrant PredyPool function remain callable during settlement? Source of LiquidationLogic not provided.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol LPs or other vault owners if tokens are drained via take()

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: Access control mismatch — execLiquidationCall restricted to privileged caller
rejected_mechanisms.claimed_locus: execLiquidationCall function signature and modifier list
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: execLiquidationCall has no access control modifier (no onlyOperator, no onlyVaultOwner, no onlyPoolOwner) — only nonReentrant. It is explicitly designed to be permissionless (anyone can liquidate). This is intentional, not a bug.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Permissionless liquidation is correct by design for DeFi lending protocols. The absence of access control here is a feature.
rejected_mechanisms.who_loses: N/A — no loss from permissionless liquidation access itself

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Potential liquidation premium via over-sized closeRatio, or tokens via malicious settlement callback
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Gas cost only — no privileged setup required
impact_direction.victim_loses: Vault owner may lose: (a) excess collateral from unconstrained closeRatio, (b) surplus margin when recipient=address(0), (c) position from premature liquidation on stale accounting
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Solvency invariant: liquidation should close only the necessary portion of a position (closeRatio bounded); accounting invariant: remaining margin must be returnable to vault owner; health-check invariant: interest must be current before solvency determination
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Victim is a real vault owner with real collateral at stake; the attack is permissionless from any EOA; surplus margin loss can be substantial depending on vault size; not admin-gated

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: three unresolved mechanisms remain that require LiquidationLogic.liquidate source or harness testing to settle — closeRatio bounds enforcement, stale interest accrual before health check, and settlement callback reentrancy path via take()
